chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A sheep suffices for the Qiran (Tamattu') Hajj.

key_terms.الْمُتْعَةِ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum animal required for the Tamattu' Hajj sacrifice in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishes the minimum valid sacrificial animal (Hadi) for Hajj al-Tamattu' as a single sheep, reflecting the practical ease (rukhas) emphasized in Shia jurisprudence. It serves as the primary textual basis for the ruling that a sheep suffices, distinguishing it from the more costly cattle required in some other schools of thought. This ruling underscores the balance between ritual obligation and economic accessibility for pilgrims.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said:
‘With regards to the Tumatto, a sheep would suffice’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya and ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
For al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) one sheep is sufficient.’”
